purpose: Research-only evidence packet for five individually registered NIAH structures in the Amiens Street and Connolly Station area

source_snapshot.queue_rule: Each selected registration number was checked as an exact entry in the workflow-generated Dublin missing-registration queue.

official_dataset_reference.title: NIAH Data Download
official_dataset_reference.note: The official national CSV provides ITM coordinates and latitude/longitude. Individual-page coordinate pairs are preserved separately as raw values because the page does not label their CRS.

candidate_records.name: Amiens Street railway bridge
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010117 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Railway bridge erected in 1891, forming part of the City of Dublin Junction Railway/Loop Line Bridge and carrying railway tracks over Amiens Street. The official NIAH description identifies a central steel span supported on piers, with masonry spans to either side and cast-iron fluted columns. It is a separately registered bridge structure, distinct from the station buildings.

candidate_records.name: Irish Rail Head Office, Connolly Station
candidate_records.address: Amiens Street / Sheriff Street Lower, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010118 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Former Great Northern Railway head office, built c.1880 to designs by John Lanyon, with a three-stage campanile to the southwest corner and a later rear extension adjoining the northwest elevation of the Connolly Station train shed. The office is a distinct registered building; its physical relationship to the station complex should be represented without merging identities.

candidate_records.name: Connolly Station
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010119 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Main station building, built 1846, originally Amiens Street Station and designed by Sir John Macneill and William Deane Butler. The NIAH describes the symmetrical granite station façade with central campanile, towers and colonnaded wings. The page notes the train shed was completed and the railway operational before the elaborate façade was finished. The station building and separately registered train shed are related but distinct.

candidate_records.name: J. & M. Cleary
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010122 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: End-of-terrace three-bay three-storey brick public house with original shopfront, built c.1900. The appraisal highlights the coved fascia with gilded signwriting and cast-iron balustrading. The record lists original use as signal box; its appraisal says it was originally built as a signal house to service the railway. Preserve the register's original-use field and note the wording difference rather than silently normalising it. The appraisal also notes a connection to James Joyce's Ulysses and use as a film location.

candidate_records.name: Connolly Station train shed
candidate_records.address: Connolly Station, Amiens Street, Dublin 1, Ireland
candidate_records.queue_membership: Exact REG_NO 50010123 present in Dublin missing-registration queue.
candidate_records.research_notes: Attached train shed built c.1850 adjoining the rear (northeast) elevation of Connolly Station. The NIAH describes its corrugated-iron and glazed roof, steel trusses, cast-iron arcade, brick and stone elevations, and surviving platform infrastructure. It is separately registered from the main station building (50010119), although physically attached.

duplicate_screen.method: Exact registration-number searches against open repository issues and pull requests.
duplicate_screen.result: No open issue or pull request matches returned for any of the five exact registration numbers at time of research.

spatial_and_identity_cautions: 50010117 is the railway bridge crossing Amiens Street; it is not the station building or the train shed.
50010118 is the former railway head office, physically associated with the Connolly Station complex but separately registered.
50010119 is the main Connolly Station building.
50010123 is the attached train shed and has its own separate NIAH registration. Do not merge it with 50010119.

50010122 is a separate terraced public house at 36 Amiens Street. Its original-use wording differs between the CSV field (signal box) and NIAH appraisal (signal house); retain both source wordings with provenance.
The five records form a geographically related transport-heritage cluster, not one single building or one undifferentiated archive object.
Individual NIAH page coordinate pairs are preserved as raw values because the page does not label their CRS. Do not interpret them as EPSG:2157 or overwrite official CSV coordinates.
NIAH descriptions of use, fabric and condition are survey-time source statements, not present-day field verification.
No physical access, ownership, public access or current condition has been verified.
explicitly_not_done: No visual inventory or source registry imports
No map pins or coordinate imports
